gap: No result ChatGPT got states that 70mai's own M310 manual forbids use above 60°C (140°F) or below -10°C and describes a built-in, non-removable 300 mAh Li-ion battery, or that 70mai's M310 page requires the separately sold UP03 hardwire kit for every parking function.
standout_why: Compared against Auto Roamer (cited), GuideSpot (cited), DashCamTalk's price tracker (cited) and DashCamTalk's M310 page. Auto Roamer already has the 300 mAh lithium battery, the separate hardwire kit and a car that 'bakes to 140 degrees Fahrenheit', but says no camera has a published operating temperature. GuideSpot says supercapacitors are superior but gives no battery, temperature or hardwire detail for the M310. The price tracker carries prices only. ChatGPT's own answer already says 'uses a lithium battery'. So the only new part is the maker's 60°C ceiling, the non-removable cell and the UP03 kit name. Dash & Drive (cited) failed to load with a certificate error, so I did not compare against it. I could not open DDPAI's side, so the battery-against-supercapacitor comparison is one-sided.
decides: It confirms the split ChatGPT already made rather than changing it. The M310 is a front-only camera whose maker caps use at 60°C, the same 140°F that Auto Roamer says a parked car reaches in summer, and its parking recording needs the UP03 kit on top of the camera price. That supports a supercapacitor camera as the hot-climate pick, which would be the DDPAI N2 Front ($49.00 in the brief's partner table; I could not re-read it today). That pick holds only if DDPAI's own stated temperature limit is higher than 60°C. A search snippet suggested DDPAI's N2 Dual page may also say 60°C; I could not open the page to check. If so, the page cannot claim a higher rated ceiling for the N2, only the absence of a lithium cell.

findings.label: Maker's operating temperature limit
findings.value: Do not use above 60°C (140°F) or below -10°C (14°F)
findings.source_title: 70mai M310 Manual (ManualsLib copy of the 70mai user manual)
findings.note: Manual text: 'Do not use this dash cam in environments with temperatures over 60°C or below -10°C.' Fahrenheit figures are my conversion. This is a ManualsLib copy; 70mai's own PDF URL returned 404 today.

findings.label: Power backup type
findings.value: Li-ion battery, 300 mAh, built in, cannot be removed or replaced; input 5 V 2 A
findings.source_title: 70mai M310 Manual (ManualsLib copy of the 70mai user manual)
findings.note: Manual text: 'This device is equipped with a built-in battery that cannot be removed or replaced.' It also warns that leaving a battery in extremely high temperature surroundings can cause explosion or leakage of flammable liquid or gas.

findings.label: Battery capacity on maker's page
findings.source_title: 70mai Dash Cam M310 (70mai official product page)
findings.note: The page gives capacity only, with no battery type and no operating temperature. It also lists sensor SC3336P, 2304 × 1296, 130° field of view and a USB Type-C power port.

findings.label: What parking recording needs
findings.value: 70mai Hardwire Kit UP03, sold separately, required for all parking surveillance functions
findings.source_title: 70mai Dash Cam M310 (70mai official product page)
findings.note: Page text: 'The 70mai Hardwire Kit UP03 is required for all parking surveillance functions, sold separately.' Also: 'The built-in G-sensor will trigger a 30s surveillance video upon collision detection.'

findings.label: Memory card the camera accepts
findings.value: microSD, 16 GB to 256 GB, Class 10 / U1 or higher
findings.source_title: 70mai M310 Manual (ManualsLib copy of the 70mai user manual)
findings.note: Manual text: 'Please use memory cards with capacity of 16GB ~ 256GB and rating of class 10, U1 or higher.' 70mai's product page gives the same 16G~256G range. Neither page lists a card in the box.

findings.label: Parking modes when hardwired (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: Collision detection (30 s clip after impact), time-lapse at 1 fps, or combined; non-buffered
findings.note: DashCamTalk's description, page published 2026-02-05. Non-buffered means the clip starts after the impact, not before it. DashCamTalk also writes that the M310 'uses a battery rather than a super capacitor making it not ideal for very high temperature environments'.

findings.label: Operating temperature in DashCamTalk's spec table
findings.note: The cold end differs from the manual's -10°C; the 60°C ceiling matches. Use the manual's figure.

findings.label: Video bitrate (DashCamTalk)
findings.note: My arithmetic: 16 Mbps = 2 MB/s = 7.2 GB per hour, so a 16 GB card holds about 2.2 hours before loop overwrite and a 256 GB card about 35 hours.

findings.label: Amazon price tracked by DashCamTalk
findings.note: The tracker says prices were last checked 2026-11-21. I did not read the Amazon listing myself. GuideSpot lists the M310 at $27.99 (page dated 2026-07-19).

findings.label: What the cited rival says about cabin heat and temperature specs
findings.value: Auto Roamer: a car 'bakes to 140 degrees Fahrenheit in summer'; it gives no operating-temperature figure for any camera
findings.source_title: Best Dash Cam Under $50 (2026): 70mai M310 Wins | Auto Roamer
findings.note: 140°F is exactly 60°C, the M310 manual's ceiling. Auto Roamer also says the M310 'runs on a small 300mAh internal lithium battery' and that its 24-hour parking surveillance 'specifically requires buying a separate hardwire kit', which it prices as 'a separate $15-25 part'.
